# Mirror of Settings > Actions > General > "Allow specified actions and reusable workflows".
#
# GitHub refuses to start a workflow that references an action outside that list, and the
# refusal arrives as `startup_failure` with no job logs — nothing names the action, so the
# workflow looks broken when the policy is what changed. Deploy sat dead for a week that way
# after Dependabot bumped azure/login and static-web-apps-deploy past their allowlisted SHAs.
#
# scripts/check-action-allowlist.ps1 fails CI when a workflow references something absent
# here, so the mismatch surfaces on the pull request that causes it rather than on main.
#
# Actions owned by `actions/` and `github/` are permitted by the github_owned_allowed setting
# and are deliberately not listed.
#
# When a Dependabot pull request changes one of these SHAs, BOTH have to move: this file, and
# the repository setting. Updating only this file makes CI pass and the deploy still fail.

gitleaks/gitleaks-action@e0c47f4f8be36e29cdc102c57e68cb5cbf0e8d1e
azure/login@f5d393ae46f8fde4be8b75f32e3fc50e654ad0ca
azure/webapps-deploy@02a81bead70021f5284939794bcec79c271ab383
Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@1a947af9992250f3bc2e68ad0754c0b0c11566c9
